name: Purple Plum
lede: Purple Plum is the library's form of Plum Purple, the colour of a ripe plum in one early list of nature's purples.

sections.title: Plum Purple in a list of purples
sections.body:
Baty's *Nature's Palette* lists Plum Purple as number 42 in a run of purples, between Auricula Purple and Red Lilac Purple [1]. The run also names Pansy Purple, Campanula Purple, Imperial Purple and Lavender Purple [1].

Each entry cites living and mineral examples. For Plum Purple the book gives the plum itself and fluor spar [1]. The neighboring Auricula Purple is also illustrated with fluor spar, which shows how close the neighbors are [1].

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: The library value is a bright violet-purple, more saturated than most ripe plums [2]. The name order is reversed in the library, and we read it as the same name as Baty's Plum Purple, which is our inference [2]. Screen colors are approximate [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The books say little more. Five passages in the concordance mention the name, all from Baty's list of purples [1].

questions.q: Which mineral does Baty pair with the plum for Plum Purple?
Plum Purple is number 42 in Baty's run of purples.

openers: In one early list of nature's purples, the plum shares its mineral example with two other purples.

issues: removed unverified claim that fluor spar also illustrates Imperial purple
